title: Word Search
description: Given an `m x n` grid of characters `board` and a string `word`, return `true` if `word` can be traced in the grid by stepping between horizontally or vertically adjacent cells. The same cell may not be used more than once in a single path.
constraints: board and word contain English letters only
hints: Any cell could be the start of the word. For each possible start, you will need to explore paths outward.
From a cell that matches the current letter, try its four neighbours for the next letter. You need a way to make sure a cell is not reused in the current path, and to undo that when you backtrack.

Write dfs(r, c, i): fail if out of bounds or the cell does not equal word[i]; succeed if i is the last index. Mark the cell as used (e.g. replace with '#'), try 4 directions, then restore the character.

solution.explanation: Try every cell as a starting point and run a depth-first search that matches word[i] at each step. When the current cell matches, temporarily mark it as visited (overwrite it with a sentinel), recurse into the four neighbours for index i + 1, and then restore the original letter so other paths can use the cell. If i reaches the end of the word we found it. Branching is at most 3 after the first step, so time is O(m * n * 3^L), with O(L) recursion depth.
